hypothesis: An abnormal one-to-three-session selloff in a liquid US equity whose slow trend is still rising can partially reverse over the next two-to-five sessions after realistic IBKR costs.
economic_rationale: Short-lived liquidity, positioning or news overreaction can move price farther than the information warrants.
Requiring price above a rising 200-session average avoids mechanically buying every persistent bear trend.
A next-open entry makes the closing shock observable and removes same-close lookahead.
Short maximum holding periods test reversal rather than silently turning the trade into long-term equity beta.

data_contract.source: Dukascopy M1 aggregated to official NYSE regular trading sessions

common_rules.normalizer: ATR(20) Wilder known at signal close
common_rules.concurrency: maximum one open position per asset and variant
common_rules.gap_exit: fill at market open if open crosses stop or target
common_rules.end_of_period: close at final period close; variants restart flat in each temporal segment

cost_and_sizing_contract.sizing: whole shares using all available realized equity, no leverage
cost_and_sizing_contract.stress: fixed commission plus 10 bps adverse slippage per side

preregistered_gates.cross_asset_promotion: A family is transferable only if the same frozen variant passes on both KO and JPM; a single-asset pass remains research-only.
preregistered_gates.multiple_testing_policy: All three preregistered variants are reported. No winner is optimized or relabelled as confirmatory.

prohibitions: No parameter optimization before all frozen results are recorded.
No Yahoo substitution for canonical Dukascopy/NYSE data.
No paper or live authorization from this screen.
